To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gene encoding oxytocin ( OT ) is highly expressed in endometrial epithelial cells during pregnancy and is also induced in the uterus during the proestrus phase of the estrus cycle and after induction by hormones.
the gene encoding oxytocin (the hypothalamic peptide) is also expressed in the endometrium, and that its expression is induced by pregnancy and the proestrus phase of the estrus cycle.
uterine oxytocin mRNA increases in the uterus at proestrus and at the time of implantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation and function of the oxytocin gene in the uterus during pregnancy and parturition.
the regulation of the oxytocin gene in the uterus.
elucidating the role of oxytocin in the regulation of uterine and ovarian function during pregnancy and parturition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OT gene is expressed at high levels in uterine epithelia of pregnant rats.
the OT gene in the uterus is induced during pregnancy, pseudopregnancy or the proestrus phase of the estrus cycle, but not in the hypothalamus.
OT gene expression in the uterus is induced by steroid hormones, whereas the OT gene is not regulated by steroids in the hypothalamus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uterine oxytocin expression is induced in a tissue-specific manner by the same steroid hormones that induce decidualization and parturition.
OT gene expression is highly up-regulated in the uterus during late pregnancy, and that the induction is dependent on a complex interaction between the uterus, hypothalamus, and pituitary.
OT gene expression is induced in the rat uterus by a steroid-dependent process that may be involved in uterine function during late pregnancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OT gene expression is induced by the proestrous rise in estradiol and is further stimulated by progesterone.
uterine oxytocin is induced in the uterus by estrogen, and it's induced by estrogen in the uterus, not in the brain.
the uterine epithelium is a site of oxytocin gene induction and expression during pregnancy and the estrous/ menstrual cycle.
